data.name: Bethara
data.gender_notes: Bethara is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, the name Bethara is derived from the words bet (house) and yarah (God). It is translated to mean 'house of God' in English. In the Bible, Bethara is the name of a town in the land of Gad where King Saul consulted the witch of Endor (1 Samuel 28:3). The name has also been associated with the daughter of Jairus, the synagogue leader, who was raised from the dead by Jesus (Mark 5:35–43).
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing devotion and faith in God.
data.etymology: Bethara belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “House of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bethara total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: בֵּיתָארָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ביתארה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשפה העברית, מורכב משני מילים: בית שפירושו בית או מקום, וארה שפירושה אור או אש, ומשמעותו היא בית האור או בית האש, ויש הטוענים כי הוא נגזר מהשם העברי בית הר, שפירושו בית ההר, והוא מוזכר בתנ״ך כאתר קדוש

in_greek.name: Βηθαρα
in_greek.long_meaning: η Βηθαρα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα, αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: το σπίτι και το φως, και η σημασία του είναι το σπίτι του φωτός ή το σπίτι της φωτιάς, και κάποιοι υποστηρίζουν ότι προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα Βηθαρ, που σημαίνει το σπίτι του βουνού, και αναφέρεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη ως ιερό μέρος

in_latin.name: Bethara
in_latin.long_meaning: Bethara est nomen christianum quod origine habet in lingua hebraica, constat ex duabus vocibus: domus et lux, et significatio eius est domus luminis vel domus ignis, et quidam asserunt quod derivatur a nomine hebraico Bethar, quod significat domus montis, et in Novo Testamento mentionem habet ut locus sanctus

in_english.name: Bethara
in_english.long_meaning: Bethara is a Christian name that originates from the Hebrew language, consisting of two words: house and light, and its meaning is house of light or house of fire, and some claim it is derived from the Hebrew name Bethar, meaning house of the mountain, and it is mentioned in the New Testament as a sacred place, symbolizing spiritual enlightenment and divine guidance

data.cultural_impact: The name "Bethara" is rooted in ancient Middle Eastern culture. It is reminiscent of the rich Biblical history of the Jewish people, adding a depth of meaning and connection to modern bearers of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Bethara" signifies the deepest commitment to serve and honor God. This is a constant reminder of the power and majesty of God and the importance of maintaining a house, or a home, that is dedicated to worshipping and loving Him. It is also a symbol of the miraculous power of God to heal, restore, and raise the dead.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bethara: House of God's Devotion. A name symbolizing deep commitment and unwavering love towards God. In the heart of a Bethara, God's presence is constant, guiding and nurturing.

biblical_reference.note: not directly mentioned in the Bible, but related to biblical concepts of light and fire

historical_references.reference: The Syriac Chronicle of 724 AD mentions Bethara as a bishopric in the province of Osrhoene, in present-day Turkey.
St. Ephrem the Syrian (306-373 AD) wrote hymns and poems that include references to Bethara as a monastic settlement in the region of Mesopotamia.

modern_usage.modern_context: Bethara is a term primarily used in the context of various spiritual and philosophical movements that draw inspiration from the Biblical figure Bethlehem, specifically the town of Bethara mentioned in the New Testament. The term 'Betharism' refers to the broader philosophical and spiritual movement, while the 'Bethara movement' and 'Bethara revival' specifically refer to contemporary groups that have adopted this ideology. Some of the core tenets of Betharism include a focus on community, simplicity, and reverence for the natural world. These ideas have found expression on various online platforms, with active communities on Reddit, Facebook, and Wikipedia, where discussions and debates around the meaning and significance of Betharism continue to evolve.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Bethara in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Bethara, which means "House of God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
